title: Knowledge check: Preparing an Express Application for Production

questions.prompt: In Preparing an Express Application for Production, which statement best describes Production environment configuration?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Validate required configuration at startup, keep credentials outside source control, expose a limited health check, and verify logs, deployment smoke tests and recovery steps before release.
Bound the request with a timeout, validate the returned shape and define an explicit failure policy. Retry only operations that are safe or protected by an idempotency mechanism.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Validate required configuration at startup, keep credentials outside source control, expose a limited health check, and verify logs, deployment smoke tests and recovery steps before release.
questions.explanation: Validate required configuration at startup, keep credentials outside source control, expose a limited health check, and verify logs, deployment smoke tests and recovery steps before release.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Preparing an Express Application for Production?
options: Production readiness includes validated environment configuration, health checks, correct proxy trust, structured logs, deployment coordination, rollback plans, and incident response. A successful local run does not prove production safety.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Production readiness includes validated environment configuration, health checks, correct proxy trust, structured logs, deployment coordination, rollback plans, and incident response. A successful local run does not prove production safety.
questions.explanation: Production readiness includes validated environment configuration, health checks, correct proxy trust, structured logs, deployment coordination, rollback plans, and incident response. A successful local run does not prove production safety.

questions.prompt: A change related to Preparing an Express Application for Production appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
